payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism in flow designs. Independent testing corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee. The cell delivers 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density, with projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its key operational limitation is a 4 °C temperature floor, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
